# Presentation Report — What Draft 2 Expands

**Author:** Nikhil Prakash (MASc, UBC ECE)
**Written:** 2026-10-10, with draft 1 (after-action report 12, step W5)
**Applies to:** `docs/presentation/REPORT_DRAFT_1.md` (generated by `make_presentation.py`) and its
published page. Draft 2 is step F1 of `docs/PLAN_WM-2.md`.

## 1. What draft 1 is, and is not
Draft 1 is complete in coverage and thin in argument. It puts every result of record in one place,
with its register row, in 10 sections, about 25 tables and 10 figures, all generated from committed data.
It does not yet explain *why* the results come out as they do, compare against prior work, or speak
to a particular audience. It also inherits every limitation of the results themselves (§7 of the draft).

## 2. Expansions, ranked by value to the thesis
| # | Expansion | Why it matters | Data or work it needs | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | **An audience and a story.** Choose the first audience (supervisor meeting, committee, or a conference talk) and re-order the draft around three to five claims that audience must leave with, each backed by one figure | a report that lists everything argues nothing | the author's choice of audience (W2 decision in the WM-2 plan) | small |
| X2 | **Why the gas ranking looks the way it does**: decompose create-identity gas into storage writes, events and calldata per standard, so the 33.7× spread is explained, not just shown | an examiner's first question about F1 | the metrics harness already counts zero-to-nonzero SSTOREs (#34–#36); a per-standard breakdown table | medium |
| X3 | **Position against prior work**: one table placing the measured numbers beside published figures (uPort/ERC-1056 costs, IEEE 1609.2 verification budgets, SCMS) with citations | the results mean little without a baseline the field recognises | chapter 2's citation set (open: N-11 lists the chapter 2 citations) | medium |
| X4 | **Interactive figures** (hover values, a table toggle) and dark-mode figure variants on the page, instead of light PNG plates | the page is for presenting; the data-viz rules expect a hover layer on HTML charts | port F1–F8 to inline SVG or a small charting library; same data | medium |

## 3. What stays the same
The generator stays the single source: every number is read from committed data, every result table
names its register row, and `--check` keeps the Markdown honest. A figure that cannot be generated
from committed data does not enter the report.

## 4. Proposed order for draft 2
X1 → X5 → X10 → X2 → X6 → X7 → X3 → X8 → X4 → X9; X11 when WM-2's re-runs land; X12 only on the
author's decisions.
